neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as an expected-count estimate for unstable slabs in the Poisson-boundary argument for wreath products. The counted lemma (label "lem: expectation of unstable points is small") fixes t0 >= 1 and finite R in B and L in A, and states that for every epsilon > 0 there is K2 > 0 with E(|U_s| given P_n^{t0}) < epsilon n + K2 for every n >= 1, where s = floor(n/t0) t0. The proof defines the slab F_j = X_{j t0} R^{t0} and the coarse neighbourhood of the trajectory, shows by the Markov property and group invariance that being poorly n0-stabilised has the same probability at every instant j (Claim 1), shows that this probability tends to 0 as n0 grows because lamp configurations stabilise almost surely (Claim 2), then splits the sum over slabs at J and obtains K2 = n0/t0 + 1.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The neighbour bounds the expected number of unstable time-slabs in a Poisson-boundary argument, as a function of a fixed window length t0 and an epsilon. Exercise 6.78 bounds from below the diagonal return probability p_{2n}(o,o) of simple random walk on the Cayley graph of the lamplighter group over Z with its standard generators, at the rate exp(-C n^{1/3}). The neighbour has no return probability, no heat-kernel diagonal, no Cayley graph of Z^odot with the standard generators and no exponent n^{1/3}; its estimate is a bounded-increment expectation whose linear term is epsilon n for an arbitrarily small epsilon, which is the opposite of a stretched-exponential lower bound. The shared vocabulary is wreath products and lamps, not the statement.
neighbor_comparisons.title: The Poisson boundary of wreath products
neighbor_comparisons.source_work: The Poisson boundary of wreath products

neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as an algebraic statement about finite quotients of a torsion-free lamplighter group. The counted lemma (label Lem::Abelian) states that the subgroup N is abelian. The proof exhibits the cofinal family Gamma(m) = C_m^n wr C_m of finite quotients with R_m = (Z/mZ)[x]/(x^m - 1), reduces via the centraliser lemma to showing that Z(m) = C_{Gamma(m)}([Gamma(m),Gamma(m)]) is abelian, and proves Z(m) = R_m^n by checking that (x^k - 1)(x - 1) is nonzero in R_m for every k, using that 1, x, ..., x^{m-1} are a Z/mZ-basis and that m > 2.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The neighbour is a group-theoretic statement: a subgroup of a torsion-free lamplighter group is abelian, proved through finite quotients and a ring computation. Exercise 6.78 is a probabilistic lower bound for a random walk transition probability. The neighbour contains no walk, no time parameter, no probability and no rate; the lamplighter group appears there as an object to be quotiented, not as a state space to be walked on. Neither statement specialises to the other.
neighbor_comparisons.title: The Profinite Rigidity of Torsion-Free Lamplighter Groups
neighbor_comparisons.source_work: The Profinite Rigidity of Torsion-Free Lamplighter Groups

neighbor_comparisons.actual_counted_statement:
\begin{proposition}\label{prop:variational}
For every $\beta\in[0,1]$, $\ \Psi(\beta)=I(\beta)$ as defined in Theorem \ref{thm:spectrum}, the maximizer is unique, and it equals
\[
(\ell_\beta,\mu_\beta)=
\Big(\tfrac{1+\beta}{2+u_r},\ \tfrac{(1+\beta)u_r}{2+u_r}\Big)\ \ (\beta\le\beta^{*}),
\qquad
(\ell_\beta,\mu_\beta)=\big(\beta,\ 1-\beta\big)\ \ (\beta\ge\beta^{*}).
\]
\end{proposition}
neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as a variational formula for the directional growth rate of the lamplighter group. The counted proposition (label prop:variational) states that for every beta in [0,1] the value Psi(beta) equals the rate function I(beta) of the article spectrum theorem, that the maximiser is unique, and that it equals ((1+beta)/(2+u_r), (1+beta)u_r/(2+u_r)) below the critical beta* and (beta, 1-beta) above it. The proof establishes positivity of the value, shows the budget constraint binds, reduces to maximising psi(u) = h(u)/(2+u) on an interval, locates the interior critical point u_r through the cubic rho^3 = rho + r, and separates the two phases at beta* = rho^3/(rho^3 + r).
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: This is the closest neighbour in subject matter, and it is still not covering. The neighbour computes an exact large-deviation rate function for the directional growth of fibre counts in the lamplighter group, together with its unique maximiser; it is a variational identity, proved by calculus on an entropy function. Exercise 6.78 asks for a lower bound on one diagonal transition probability of a random walk on the same group, at the rate exp(-C n^{1/3}). The neighbour has no random walk, no transition probability and no heat kernel; a growth rate along a direction does not bound a return probability in either direction, and the exponent n^{1/3} does not appear. The relevance is thematic, not logical.
neighbor_comparisons.title: A phase transition in the directional growth\\ of lamplighter groups
neighbor_comparisons.source_work: A phase transition in the directional growth\\ of lamplighter groups

neighbor_comparisons.actual_core_read: Read as an eigenfunction completeness identity for the heat kernel of a Cayley graph. The counted proposition (label completeness1) states that for all integers m, n the sum of f_epsilon(m) f_epsilon(n) over epsilon plus the integral over x of the continuous family against dx/H_{mu epsilon}(x) equals the Kronecker delta. The proof reduces by a symmetry relation to the case C(2m,2n+1) with m,n >= 0, computes F_x(2m,2n+1) explicitly, expands the denominator 4cos(2x) - 5 by a partial-fraction and geometric-series decomposition, evaluates the integral against cosines, and shows the total is 0.
neighbor_comparisons.reason_target_distinct: The neighbour is a completeness (orthonormality) identity for a family of eigenfunctions of a heat kernel on a Cayley graph, established by explicit Fourier-type computation on PSL_2(Z). Exercise 6.78 is a lower bound for the diagonal of the transition probability of a different random walk on a different group. The neighbour asserts that a spectral family is complete; it gives no decay rate for any transition probability, and it concerns a non-amenable group with a completely different spectral picture from the lamplighter group. Despite the shared words heat kernel and Cayley graph, the statements do not overlap.
neighbor_comparisons.title: On the heat kernel of a Cayley graph of $\operatorname{PSL}_2\mathbb{Z}$: the completeness of the eigenfunction family
neighbor_comparisons.source_work: On the heat kernel of a Cayley graph of $\operatorname{PSL}_2\mathbb{Z}$
